mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for 6 months but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals rising manufacturing output, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO rises > 0.5% for 3 months but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.25% signals tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% for 2 months but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.3% signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.3% for 1 month but S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis is falsified.
